blocks.text: Compose runs one application on one host; Kubernetes continuously reconciles many applications across many hosts. Move when you need multi-node availability, rolling deploys or autoscaling, not because of service count.

rows: Rolling updates, replicas, stable virtual IP
RBAC, encryption at rest, external operators

items: HA across machines; zero-downtime deploys required; autoscaling; many teams on shared policy-driven infra.

blocks.text: A single VM with Compose, backups, monitoring and a proxy runs plenty of production. Managed platforms (Cloud Run, ECS Fargate, Container Apps, Fly.io) give rolling deploys and autoscaling without running a cluster.
Immutable images, env/secret config, stateless containers, /healthz and /readyz, SIGTERM handling, stdout logs, startup retries.

Q: "When would you move from Compose to Kubernetes?" A: "When requirements exceed one host: multi-node high availability, zero-downtime rolling deploys, autoscaling or shared multi-team infrastructure. Otherwise a single VM or a managed container platform is simpler. Twelve-factor apps move with just new manifests."

items: Kubernetes has no depends_on: apps must retry.
Managed platforms are a middle ground.
